strings.name: Drew Weissman
strings.summary: Weissman studies immunity and RNA technology. With Katalin Karikó, he showed that nucleoside modifications could reduce inflammation caused by introduced mRNA and improve protein production. Their work underpinned later mRNA vaccine platforms and earned the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Developing and distributing vaccines also required many other teams, clinical trials and manufacturing systems.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Key modified-mRNA discoveries
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: With Karikó and colleagues, showed that nucleoside modifications could reduce unwanted innate immune responses.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Foundations for vaccine platforms
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: The discoveries supported COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and other RNA research, rather than constituting the entire vaccine-development process.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Shared his research journey
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Explained mRNA research and scientific discovery to students at Germantown Friends School.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Shared the Nobel Prize
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Awarded with Karikó for nucleoside-modification discoveries enabling effective COVID-19 mRNA vaccines.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Improved protein production
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The team reported that pseudouridine-containing mRNA increased protein output while reducing immune stimulation.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Published modification research
strings.timeline.event-04.text: With Karikó and colleagues, found that changing RNA building blocks reduced inflammatory responses in dendritic cells.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Joined the University of Pennsylvania
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Established RNA and vaccine research and subsequently collaborated with Karikó.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Completed medical and doctoral training
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Earned MD and PhD degrees at Boston University before further clinical and immunology training.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Completed undergraduate studies
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Graduated from Brandeis, studying biochemistry and enzymology.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Born in Lexington
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Born and raised in Massachusetts, United States.
